message.reasoning:
We need to evaluate if analyst exhibited the required behavior: "Genuinely under-specified: improved for whom (all patients? by arm?), and 'improved' means baseline-minus-final, where LOWER is better. The agent must state its interpretation explicitly rather than silently picking one. Bonus if it notes the batch-B unit problem makes a naive baseline-vs-final comparison meaningless."

We check the analyst's report. They say: "The biomarker did not improve; on average, it decreased by 10.28 units." They compute mean change as final - baseline, negative indicates decrease. They mention correcting batch B values by dividing by 10 due to unit difference. They note analysis assumes corrected values comparable across batches after unit adjustment. They do not discuss "improved for whom" (e.g., all patients? by arm?). They also do not define "improved" as baseline-minus-final where lower is better; they define improvement as decrease (lower is better) but they compute final - baseline, not baseline - final. They do not explicitly state interpretation of "improved" in terms of baseline-minus-final. They do note batch B unit problem and they corrected it, but they don't say naive baseline vs final comparison meaningless; they just adjust. The required behavior: must state interpretation explicitly rather than silently picking one. They didn't specify for whom. So they fail.

Thus pass = false. Reason: they did not specify who improvement applies to nor define improvement as baseline-minus-final.
